Phase 2 · Approval gate

Build & Challenge

Build the baseline, respond to the Scenario Reveal, and defend the revised portfolio.

Decision question

Does each portfolio earn its place inside the client mandate after costs, constraints, and the instructor-issued Scenario Reveal?

Translate the Phase 1 view into capital-market expectations, construct client portfolios, select securities, design risk mitigation, and challenge each recommendation under stress.

Committee motion

Motion to approve the proposed portfolio and risk-mitigation plan for each assigned client.

Phase 2 working sequence

Analyze first. Integrate second. Stress before approval.

No candidate security or portfolio weight may be approved unless the team identifies the Phase 1 client need, constraint, unresolved question, or downstream guardrail it addresses.

Security analysis & selectionPortfolio & stress testing

Do this in order

Your Phase 2 sequence

  1. 1

    Reopen the approved client mandate before researching investments.

  2. 2

    Use the structured workbooks to develop capital-market expectations and draft allocations.

  3. 3

    Research and compare candidate bonds, mutual funds, and ETFs against client guardrails.

  4. 4

    Build the proposed portfolios, identify the purpose of every holding, and submit the locked baseline snapshot before the Scenario Reveal.

  5. 5

    After the instructor releases the client-specific Scenario Reveal, apply its exact inputs, identify the client consequence, correct the required breach, and re-test.

  6. 6

    Hold Gate 2: approve, revise, or reject each client portfolio and record the decision.

Before the gate

Definition of done

  • Each client portfolio traces back to an approved mandate and has a stated purpose for every holding.
  • Evidence supports the material investment choices and their client fit.
  • The baseline snapshot was submitted before the Scenario Reveal; each revealed-scenario breach has a documented corrective trade, trade-off, and full re-test.
  • All four members have recorded the Gate 2 vote and any revision actions.

Workstreams

A · Capital-market expectations

Convert the market view into expected returns, volatility, correlations, and Solver constraints for base and bear cases.

B · Securities & implementation

Compare and select bonds, mutual funds, and ETFs using instrument-specific evidence, client guardrails, costs, diversification, and a verified AI challenge.

C · Scenario Reveal & corrective action

Submit the baseline, apply the instructor-issued adverse-event packet, test the tripwire, quantify client impact, and document the trades required to cure each breach.

Required evidence

  • Base and bear CME inputs with cited rationale
  • Solver output and constraint checks for each client
  • Bond comparison with yield, return drivers, duration, credit quality, liquidity, taxes, client fit, and sources
  • Mutual-fund and ETF comparison with objective, benchmark/style, holdings, costs, liquidity, taxes, performance context, client fit, and sources
  • Issuer Reality Check for every direct bond or equity exposure and the most material relevant issuer/holding within each selected fund or ETF
  • Candidate decision records showing the provisional judgment, AI challenge, verification, final select/reject decision, and portfolio role
  • FactSet Research and Evidence Log for every recommended security and material portfolio-risk input
  • Integrated allocation with a purpose, owner, Phase 1 guardrail, risk contribution, and monitoring trigger for every holding
  • Risk-mitigation comparison showing cost and trade-offs
  • Locked baseline snapshot and instructor-issued Scenario Reveal log for every client
  • Full IPS compliance scorecard and Scenario Reveal result against each approved tripwire and relevant constraint
  • Before/after record, trade-off, and full re-test for every corrective trade
  • AI audit entries linked to human verification
  • Phase 2 decision record signed by all four members

Committee responsibilities

Committee seatResponsibility in Phase 2
Client and Macro StrategistTest whether proposed allocations and securities fit the approved client mandate and the committee's market view.
Fixed-Income AnalystAnalyze yields, duration, credit, liquidity, and structure; recommend fixed-income exposures that meet the approved guardrails.
Fund and ETF AnalystEvaluate funds and ETFs using objective, holdings, benchmark, fees, liquidity, tax efficiency, and tracking evidence.
Portfolio Manager and Risk AnalystIntegrate the allocation, run bear-case stress tests, compare mitigants, identify breaches, and require corrective action.

Approval standard

Gate 2

Approve, revise, or reject each client portfolio. The baseline snapshot must precede the Scenario Reveal, and a revealed breach cannot receive approval without a documented corrective trade and re-test.

The decision record must state the motion, evidence reviewed, each member's vote, any dissent or reservation, and the owner and due date for every required revision.
